issues.legal_issue: A prior assessment of income in the hands of one person does not prevent the tax authority from assessing the person who is legally liable for that income under the applicable income-tax law.
material_facts: Two individuals jointly purchased land and shared the compensation received when it was acquired.
The tax authority had previously assessed each individual's share of the compensation in that individual's own hands for other assessment years.
The tax authority later proposed to assess the joint activity as an association of persons for the same income, and the respondent challenged its authority to do so.
issues.conclusion: The prior assessments in the individuals’ hands did not bar assessment of the association of persons if it was the person legally liable for the income. The appeal was allowed and the High Court’s judgment was set aside; the Court expressed no opinion on the respondent’s other objections.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(1) and 2(31) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, tax is charged on the person legally liable for the income; those provisions give the assessing officer no option to tax either an association of persons or its members individually. The contrast with Section 3 of the Income Tax Act, 1922, which expressly allowed that choice, supports this construction. Section 183 of the 1961 Act also shows that Parliament expressly provided a choice where it intended one. The decisions in Mahendra Kumar Agarwal v. Income Tax Officer, Rodamal Lalchand v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Choudry Brothers v. Commissioner of Income Tax, and Punjab Cloth Stores v. Commissioner of Income Tax were consistent with this view. The contrary decisions in Commissioner of Income Tax v. Blue Mountain Engineering Corporation and Commissioner of Income Tax v. Pure Nichitpur Colliery Company were not followed. Ramanlal Madanlal v. Commissioner of Income Tax recognized the distinction between the two Acts in the context of an unregistered firm. Commissioner of Income Tax v. Kanpur Coal Syndicate and Commissioner of Income Tax v. Murlidhar Jhawar and Purna Ginning and Pressing Factory were decided under the 1922 Act and did not determine the issue under the different language of the 1961 Act.

predicates.tax_assessment_proceeding: A tax authority initiated or pursued a proceeding to assess income for tax.
predicates.income_legally_belongs_to_assessee: The income was legally taxable to the person whom the authority sought to assess.
predicates.same_income_assessed_to_other_person: The same income had previously been assessed in the hands of a different person.

issues.definition: When a tax assessment proceeding concerns income legally taxable to the person being assessed, a prior assessment of that same income to someone else does not prevent the authority from assessing the legally liable person.
